newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Wills aims for market share over 30 pct.
newsitem.headline: Wills aims for market share over 30 pct.

text.p: Tobacco group W.D.& H.O. Wills Holdings Ltd Chairman Nick Greiner said on Thursday he was hopeful the group could increase its ex-factory market share to above 30 percent by the end of calendar 1997 from its current 29.3 percent.
Greiner said that full year profits would be obviously higher if the group achieved its market share goal.

Greiner said any settlement between the major U.S. tobacco companies and state authorities would not have any immediate implications for the Australian market but that in the longer term a flow on effect could not be ruled out.
Earlier, Wills director Paul Adams, who is also a director of board B.A.T. Industries Plc board, told Reuters the parent company had no comment on the speculation of a U.S. settlement.
B.A.T., which holds 67 percent of W.D. & H.O. Wills, owns Brown and Williamson, the United States' third largest tobacco group.
